title: SWAT Team Responds to Man's 3rd Bank Robbery
description:
Submit a tip! Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

The main suspect, Matthew McCloskey, was charged with bank robbery and kidnapping. He had multiple prior bank robbery convictions in New York, one in 2013 and another in 2016, marking him as a repeat offender. McCloskey stole $877 from the bank, an amount he was later ordered to repay in restitution. The case was investigated by the Waycross Police Department and the FBI, resulting in a successful prosecution in U.S. federal court. He was ultimately given 14 years in federal prison and placed under three years of supervised release. As FBI agent Will Clark later stated, by now, Matthew McCloskey should realize robbing a bank is not a winning proposition. The getaway driver Stephen Hamm was also charged with armed robbery and held in Ware County Jail without bond for his involvement. That's what happens when a crime is under federal eyes, coordinated investigators, and a system that doesn't stop once your name hits their desk. It's never an easy payday, that's consequences in a timeline with nowhere to run. Bank robberies are not street-level crimes. They travel because, unlike a spontaneous street robbery, they immediately generate federal-level documentation and multi-agency involvement so the crime moves with the suspect. Law enforcement comes through cameras, witness statements, license plates, and all digital footprints. This is how investigation stack evidence across space and time. And what stands out here isn't just the investigation, it's everything that comes after. The resistance coupled with the victim mentality, that's not strength. That's a man realizing the story he thought he controlled is down being written by witnesses and evidence pointing straight to him. Remember this, banks don't just record what you did and remember who you are and the system that follows, it doesn't lose track.
